summary: Executed backend + frontend verification for Internal Data AI security/correctness refactor. Added a dedicated 19-test pytest suite with MOCKED MongoDB/intent paths and one optional live smoke. 17 tests passed; 2 critical backend issues remain.

critical.issue: Scope normalization is case-sensitive ("Scope 1" is not normalized), so scoped analytics can return zero records even when matching data exists.
Version-history query to esg_responses_versions lacks organization_id filter, allowing cross-org/global version reads.

action_items: Fix analytics scope parsing to normalize scope values case-insensitively before regex filtering (accept 'Scope 1', 'scope 1', '1').
Add organization scoping (and facility-aware scoping where applicable) to esg_responses_versions query in get_framework_version_history.
critical_code_review_comments: Security: get_framework_version_history currently builds version query only from record/question IDs and misses explicit organization boundary.
Correctness: analytics.query scope parsing diverges from emissions.search_records behavior; normalization should be consistent across services.
seed_data_creation: None (only read operations plus internal_ai_conversations write from optional live chat smoke).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Unit coverage includes org/facility scope helpers, deterministic period parsing, router period authority override, planner/executor formula chain, formula exact-id lookup, evidence/history scoping, and optional live /api/internal-ai/chat smoke. MOCKED paths used for deterministic isolation: OpenAI intent behavior and MongoDB fixtures. Current remaining failures are exactly: analytics scope normalization with 'Scope 1' and framework version query org filter.
rca of the issue: 1) analytics.query builds scope regex via scope.replace('scope ', '') which is case-sensitive; input 'Scope 1' remains unchanged and fails against stored scope='1', causing false no-data. Mitigation: normalize scope with lower() or regex extraction before query build. 2) get_framework_version_history constrains source esg_responses by org, but follow-up esg_responses_versions query only uses record_id/question_key and omits organization_id. Mitigation: include organization_id in version query and preserve fail-closed behavior when record_id/question_key sets are empty.
